newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close down on futures expiry.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close down on futures expiry.

text.p: French shares closed with a sharp loss, affected by a further 55 point fall in the Dow Jones Industrial Index on Wall Street and profit-taking on the expiry of February futures, dealers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 21.85 points or 0.83 percent at 2,607.55 at while the CAC-40 March futures contract was down at 2,625 from 2,640 on Thursday's close.
Volume was 8.5 billion francs of which 6.4 billion on CAC-40 shares. GAN was suspended and Renault closed 13 percent higher at 146.90 francs after its Belgian plant closure announcement.
* The publication of U.S. fourth quarter GDP data in the afternoon had little impact.

* AGF closed four percent down at 200.50 francs as speculation about a bid for it faded and amid market talk it could itself be interested in the insurance business of GAN which will be bailed out by a 20 billion franc state package.

* GAN was suspended at 149.10 francs, after a 21.22 percent rise. "Obviously the market's assumption is that the government is pretty much writing out a blank cheque and not diluting shareholders," one insurance analyst said.

* LVMH, down 4.99 percent at 1,333 francs, said the DFS buy would slightly dilute 1996 net results. LVMH also said it was in talks with remaining DFS minority holder Robert Miller -- who had previously objected to a deal between LVMH and other holders -- and expected these discussions could end soon at terms close to the original buy.
* Schneider was down 3.04 percent at 300.10. On Thursday it agreed to a deal to sell Spie Batignolles to management and AMEC Plc.

* Alcatel closed 1.02 percent lower at 585 francs. The company said it was filing of FCC approval for a $3.5 billion low-orbit multimedia satellite project for which it needed to find financial and industrial partners.
